title: two one-element arrays compare as equal in an optimized build when a struct's __deinit__ prints
compiler: prints `del 1`, `del 2`, `True False` in a default build: the arrays compare as equal whatever they hold. With -O0 or -D ASSERT=all it prints the right `False True`. The answers are right when the destructor is `pass`, when the values come from parameters or pop, with two-element arrays, and with plain Ints
fixed: compares the elements one by one, as the pin does at -O0 and in every control, so it prints `del 1`, `del 2`, `False True`

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular

nightly.result: prints `True False`, as the pin does; Mojo 1.2.0 and the nightly 1.3.0.dev2026111705 do too
